detected_issues.value: 0.34 x leg length ahead of hip
detected_issues.recommendation: The foot is landing ~34% of a leg length ahead of the hip at contact. This brakes each step and raises impact load. Increasing cadence toward 170-190 spm and landing with the foot closer under the hip reduces overstride.

analysis_confidence.explanation: Pose tracking occasionally confused the left and right legs; leg-based metrics may be less precise. Try a clearer video with the whole body in frame, or film from a different angle.

capture_report.headline: This is almost always a symptom of how few pixels of you there were (the row above) rather than a fault of its own. If that was fine, the other two causes are a body reading as a dark silhouette -- keep the light behind the camera, not behind the athlete -- and a view almost exactly side-on, where a few degrees of angle helps separate the legs.

checks.target: under 5% -- on a well-framed clip this sits near zero

checks.label: How steady the camera was
checks.measured: camera moved 34% as much as your hips did (23.5 px)
checks.target: under 15% -- a camera on a tripod or a fence post reads near zero
checks.action: Rest the phone on something, or lean against a wall. Vertical oscillation is measured as your hips rising and falling in the frame, so a camera that rises and falls with the operator's breathing or footsteps adds itself to the reading -- and it does it at roughly your step frequency, which is why it cannot simply be filtered out.

checks.label: How much of the frame you fill
checks.measured: 908 px tall (71% of the frame height)
checks.target: 550 px or more -- roughly two thirds of the frame height

checks.label: The angle you filmed from
checks.target: filmed square-on to your side, so the joints move across the lens

checks.label: Which way you held the phone
checks.target: portrait -- a tall frame puts nearly twice the pixels on your legs

issues.label: Overstride
issues.problem: Overstriding -- foot lands 0.3x leg length ahead of the hip (optimal under 0.15)
issues.instruction: Run 4x20 seconds at a deliberately higher step rate on a metronome set to 180 bpm, focusing on landing with the foot under your hips rather than reaching out in front.
issues.cue: Land under your body, not out in front -- shorter, quicker steps

title: Running, treadmill, side view
blurb: A 9-second treadmill clip, framed so the athlete fills it. Every stride metric measured: cadence, ground contact, flight time, vertical oscillation and overstride, plus the five kinogram positions.
